bad_decomposition_pattern: Merge worker/index.js and worker/mcp/server.js under a single 'Cloudflare Worker Code' component owning all of node:32f3a0d3845cf98fb8cb, node:javascript_import:worker.mcp.server, and node:1e8ba7fd1db36d8f49db, then drop contract:router-to-mcp because from_component_id and to_component_id would resolve to the same merged component.
expected_gate_failure: Contract graph integrity check: contract:router-to-mcp declares from_component_id=comp:worker-edge-router and to_component_id=comp:mcp-server. If both are merged into one component, either both IDs point to a non-existent component (the merged one has a new ID) or the contract becomes a self-referential edge with from==to. Any gate validating that from_component_id != to_component_id and that both referenced IDs exist in the components list rejects this decomposition deterministically.
why_hidden_from_primary: The primary decomposer (claude-opus-4-8) was given distinct source nodes for worker/index.js and worker/mcp/server.js and correctly split them on semantic responsibility. A file-bucket report generator grouping by filesystem directory (worker/) rather than by semantic boundary would bundle them. The probe tests whether the directed-contract endpoint distinctness invariant is enforced, not just whether files are listed.

bad_decomposition_pattern: Move all ten persona corpus node IDs (node:270b52766ba2097c3bf8, node:087085bf23e3cc4628f2, node:3497d88db26b2742c66a, node:5ea405faea230cdf5498, node:7ad8da6a627ab8d27e9e, node:9d9d37a18c7ab7537c0f, node:c627dcac9798554af877, node:ca0aad13b3b497dd9e40, node:cd8a921454b74ef09e06, node:f0fd663527865f98c64e) into comp:public-agent-data's owned_node_ids on the grounds that represent_me.md is 'agent-facing content analogous to llms.txt', eliminate comp:persona-corpus as a distinct component, and repoint contract:build-renders-persona to to_component_id=comp:public-agent-data.
expected_gate_failure: Near-neighbor alternative nn:persona-in-data is explicitly marked why_not_primary='prompt/represent_me.md is a distinct prose corpus with separate prov; it is authored representation guidance, not machine-readable API data.' A gate that checks whether any near_neighbor_alternative's rejected pattern is instantiated in the decomposition detects this. Additionally, a prov-node-to-component uniqueness check fails: persona prov refs (prov:756f566ef137b772 and siblings) conflict with comp:public-agent-data's prov refs (prov:5dd0cc494cd85fbe, prov:77b106b079f49cac), producing a multi-component prov collision.
why_hidden_from_primary: The primary correctly distinguished machine-readable data (JSON, llms.txt) from prose corpus (Markdown sections with narrative structure). A generator classifying by consumer role ('both are agent-facing') rather than artifact type and authoring surface would merge them. The probe tests the near-neighbor exclusion gate and prov-uniqueness check.

bad_decomposition_pattern: Add invented dist/ directory graph nodes to comp:build-pipeline's owned_node_ids with the rationale that 'the pipeline produces and therefore owns its output,' citing no prov refs for the added nodes.
expected_gate_failure: Two gates fire. First, the non-goal enforcement gate checks that no owned_node_id resolves to a generated output surface; the project packet records surface_counts.generated=0, so any node corresponding to a dist/ artifact has no matching packet entry and fails this check. Second, the anti-fabrication concern (concern:anti-fabrication, triggered_by='universal') requires that every component's owned_node_ids trace to packet-supplied prov identifiers; dist/ nodes carry no prov ref and the anti-fabrication gate emits a fabricated-node violation.
why_hidden_from_primary: The primary correctly scoped ownership to scripts/build.py and its packet-anchored prov. A naive generator conflating 'build pipeline' with 'everything the build touches or emits' would claim dist/ nodes. The probe tests both non-goal enforcement and anti-fabrication prov anchoring simultaneously.

bad_decomposition_pattern: Remove concern:anti-fabrication from cross_cutting_concerns entirely, or reduce its component_ids to only ['comp:build-pipeline'] with triggered_by='conditional' on the rationale that 'fabrication risk is highest where data edges are missing (build pipeline only).'
expected_gate_failure: Universal-concern coverage assertion: enumerate all seven component IDs from the components list; collect all cross_cutting_concerns with triggered_by='universal' and union their component_ids. With concern:anti-fabrication absent or scoped, only concern:provenance (if left universal) covers some components. Five component IDs—comp:link-checker, comp:worker-edge-router, comp:mcp-server, comp:persona-corpus, comp:project-docs—have no universal-concern coverage. The gate diffs the full component ID set against universally-covered IDs and emits a non-empty gap set, causing deterministic failure without any network call or model invocation.
why_hidden_from_primary: The primary modeled anti-fabrication correctly as universal. A file-bucket report generator would not model cross-cutting concerns at all, or would scope them narrowly to where graph edges explicitly surface the risk. The probe tests universal-coverage enforcement across all seven components.
